- Scheme: A (this is an OIML Certificate of Conformity issued under the MAA — scheme A, since it's an Issuing Authority NMi Certin B.V., OIML Issuing Authority NL1). The schema asks scheme (A|B). This cert says "OIML Issuing Authority NL1" which indicates scheme A (Issuing Authority certificates). Actually, OIML-CS has two schemes: A (certificates issued by Issuing Authorities) and B (by Member States' bodies without issuing authority status). NMi Certin B.V. is OIML Issuing Authority NL1, so scheme A.

Certified type:
- category: "Non-automatic weighing instrument" — the schema category examples include "Load cell", "Indicator", ... For R76 the category is "Non-automatic weighing instrument". Use that.
- type_designations: ["InBody 770"]
- module_designation: null / omit — probably "Not applicable" — I'll omit or set null. Schema says "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. I'll include "Not applicable"? Actually for indicators it's not applicable. Safer to omit or null. The instruction: don't fabricate. I'll set module_designation: null. Hmm, including null is fine.
- description: "Intended to be used for weighing patients" — that's an application; could go into description or characteristics. I could add description "Non-automatic weighing instrument intended to be used for weighing patients". Actually the Application row is part of characteristics. The schema characteristics.type_level is for attributes with value/unit. Application is a string attribute. I can include it as type_level attribute with value string "Intended to be used for weighing patients". The structured value shape allows value as string. unit_symbol null.

Model family: single type InBody 770 — no multiple variants. So omit model_family? The schema says include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. So omit.

Characteristics type_level:
- accuracy_class: "(III)" → value "III", string. unit null.
- maximum_capacity: "Max ≤ 270 kg" → value {min: null, max: 270}, unit "kg".
- verification_scale_interval: "e ≥ 100 g" → value {min: 100, max: null}, unit "g".
- maximum_number_of_scale_intervals: "n ≤ 2700 divisions" → value {min: null, max: 2700}, unit "divisions" or null? "divisions" isn't a unit symbol per se but I can keep unit_symbol "divisions" or null. I'll use null and value {min:null, max:2700}? Hmm, "divisions" is a counting unit; keep unit_symbol "divisions" is fine but unitsdb lookup... rule says leave unit_id null unless certain. I'll set unit_symbol: "divisions". Actually maybe safer: value: 2700 with max? It says n ≤ 2700 divisions. So value {min: null, max: 2700}.
- temperature_range: "+5 °C / +35 °C" → {min: 5, max: 35}, unit "°C".
- weighing_ranges: "Single interval" → string value. attribute weighing_range or weighing_ranges: value "Single interval".
- power supply: "Adapter 100 – 240 V AC 50/60 Hz to 12 V DC" → split:
  - power_supply_voltage: {min: 100, max: 240}, unit "V"
  - power_supply_frequency: {min: 50, max: 60}, unit "Hz"
  - power_supply_type: "AC" (input) — but there's also DC output 12 V. Hmm. The adapter: input 100-240 V AC 50/60 Hz, output 12 V DC. So:
  - power_supply_type: "AC"
  - power_supply_output_voltage: 12, unit "V"
  - power_supply_output_type: "DC"
  Maybe simpler: power_supply_voltage: {min:100,max:240}, unit V; power_supply_frequency {50,60} Hz; power_supply_type "AC"; adapter_output_voltage 12 V DC. I'll include power_supply_voltage (input) and power_supply_frequency and power_supply_type AC and output_voltage 12 V with DC. Let me name:
  - power_supply_voltage: {min:100, max:240}, "V"
  - power_supply_frequency: {min:50, max:60}, "Hz"
  - power_supply_type: "AC"
  - power_supply_output_voltage: 12, "V"
  - power_supply_output_type: "DC"
  That's detailed. Or just note adapter. I'll include those.
- software_identification: "Version number: \"IB770-1.0(Lock)\"" → value "IB770-1.0(Lock)" with attribute software_version maybe. I'll use software_identification: value "IB770-1.0(Lock)".
- application: "Intended to be used for weighing patients" → string value.
